input: Draft a business card design for my freelance brand

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Business cards can range from a simple single-sided text layout to a double-sided design with logos, QR codes, or custom illustrations — knowing what elements to include shapes the entire design.
The target audience (e.g., corporate clients, creatives, local businesses) determines the tone, formality, and visual language of the card.
Whether this is for print, digital sharing (e.g., a PDF or image), or both affects format, resolution, bleed margins, and file output requirements.
An existing logo, brand colors, or fonts must be incorporated; if none exist, the design needs to establish those from scratch, which is a much larger task.
Visual style preferences — minimal, bold, elegant, playful — directly drive layout, typography, and color choices.
Knowing what 'done well' means — e.g., a final print-ready file, a mood board, a written design brief, or a rough mockup — defines the deliverable.
The tool or format used (e.g., Canva, Adobe Illustrator, a written spec) depends on the user's skill level and what they plan to hand off to a printer or designer.

gold.taskTitle: Draft a Freelance Brand Business Card Design
gold.taskDescription: Create a business card design concept that reflects the user's freelance brand identity, ready for print or digital use.

questions.title: What field or industry is your freelance work in?
questions.description: Knowing whether the user is a photographer, developer, consultant, designer, etc. determines the visual tone and the information hierarchy on the card.

questions.title: Which specific elements should appear on the card?
questions.description: Clarify whether to include a logo, job title, phone number, website, social handles, QR code, tagline, or any other content.

questions.title: Will this card be printed, shared digitally, or both?
questions.description: Determines output format requirements such as bleed, resolution, CMYK vs. RGB, and file type.

questions.title: Do you already have a logo, brand colors, or fonts to use?
questions.description: Establishes whether existing brand assets must be incorporated or whether a visual identity needs to be created alongside the card.

questions.title: What visual style best describes your brand's personality?
questions.description: Captures aesthetic preferences such as minimal, bold, elegant, playful, or corporate to guide layout and typography decisions.

questions.title: What does a finished, usable deliverable look like to you?
questions.description: Clarifies whether the user needs a print-ready file, a written design brief, a Canva mockup, or a conceptual layout they can hand to a designer.

questions.title: Which tool do you plan to use to build the final design?
questions.description: Knowing the tool — Canva, Adobe Illustrator, Figma, or outsourcing to a designer — shapes the format of the plan and the guidance provided.
